URL: https://www.independent.co.uk/news/uk/politics/hmrc-tax-bank-accounts-healey-budget-b3072948.html
The Independent — datePublished and dateModified both 2026-10-25T14:07:02Z = 14:07 GMT Sun 25 Oct. Retrieved by curl at 17:35 GMT.

HEADLINE SENSE: HMRC to be given power to take money directly from the bank accounts of tax evaders, expected to be announced at Wednesday's Budget.

PROVENANCE — THIS IS A SECOND-HAND TRAIL
The Independent's sourcing is explicit: "HM Revenue & Customs (HMRC) will have the authority to deduct money from current and savings accounts of people who fail to pay their tax bill, The Times reported." The original is The Times, which is an approved source but is not retrievable from here (thetimes.com 403s). The Independent is the retrievable carrier.

ON THE RECORD
Andrew Griffith, shadow chancellor, told The Times the move was "absurd", accusing Labour of giving the taxman the power "to empty your bank account over a few hundred pounds and leave you with nothing to pay the rent".
The Treasury, to The Independent: "As has always been the case, decisions on tax are a matter for the chancellor to set out at fiscal events, rather than routinely commenting on rumour, speculation or proposals." This is a non-confirmation and should be read as one.
The Association of Taxation Technicians told The Times that HMRC should not introduce the powers until it can give assurance that adequate safeguards are in place and the right taxpayers would be targeted.

FIGURES AS CARRIED
Britain's tax debt: £60bn.
"HMRC estimates that around 4.8 million people and companies hold debts below £10,000, totalling about £4bn," an average of £950 for individual customers. [4.8m x £950 = £4.56bn, not £4bn. The two figures in this sentence do not reconcile exactly; the £4bn and the £950 average cannot both be right for 4.8m holders. Do not run both numbers in the same sentence.]
Existing powers: HMRC can already take money directly from accounts of debtors owing more than £1,000 in tax, provided at least £5,000 remains after recovery. "These powers, which came into force in 2015, were paused during the pandemic and reintroduced by Labour in 2025." The threshold "could be slashed to as little as a few pounds" for repeat non-payers, and deductions could include fines and interest.
NAO (approved source): HMRC "is facing increasing issues from debtors who do not engage with it". Since 2021 HMRC has recruited more staff, increased use of private debt collection agencies and used data to tailor its approach, generating an estimated £10.7bn in additional revenue by the end of 2025-26 against spending of £368m.

SEPARATE BUDGET TRAIL IN THE SAME PIECE, ALSO SOURCED TO REPORTING NOT ANNOUNCEMENT
Online marketplaces such as Amazon, eBay and Temu to be made responsible for collecting tax owed by retailers selling on their platforms, aimed mainly at foreign sellers avoiding VAT, "expected to raise as much as £1bn, money which will be used to cut business rates for high street shops". Framed by the Independent as "rumoured" and "reportedly".
The TUC has called on the prime minister to introduce a windfall tax on banks and use the money to cut energy bills with a social tariff for two in three households.
